_source: Five Parsecs From Home: Compendium, Bug Hunt. Main Rules printed pp.177-180 and Battle Round pp.198-201, with Combat Teams p.173. Read from the PDF with PyPDF2 (printed page N = reader.pages[N+1]) on 2026-10-30. The wording is the book's, shortened; every number is as printed.
description: The Bug Hunt battle rules a player looks up mid-battle. Rendered as the battle screen's Reference tab in a Bug Hunt battle (CheatSheetSections.bug_hunt_sections). The weapon table is not repeated here: it is read from bug_hunt_weapons.json (p.179).

sections.title: Battle Round
lines: Four phases each round: 1. Quick Action, 2. Enemy Action, 3. Slow Action, 4. Spawn.
Roll one D6 for each main character and each combat team, and assign one die to each.
A die equal to or below the Reaction score acts in the Quick Action phase; above it, in the Slow Action phase. Every figure still acts each round.
A combat team rolls a single die, and every figure in it acts in the same phase. A team in formation (every member within 2" of one chosen member) gets +1 to its Reaction score (p.173).
All enemies act in the Enemy Action phase, nearest to a player figure first.

sections.title: Actions and Snap Fire
lines: A figure may Move and then take a Combat Action (fire, or fight a Brawl), never in the reverse order.
A Stunned trooper may Move OR take a Combat Action, not both. A Stunned enemy stays in place and takes no actions. Remove 1 Stun marker after the figure acts.

Snap Fire: a trooper eligible for the Quick Action phase may hold, to fire when an opponent moves or to act in the Slow Action phase. A target Stunned while moving loses its other actions this round. Firing during an opponent's move stops the firer moving this round.
A held trooper who found no chance to fire may Move or Fire in the Slow Action phase, not both. Enemies carry no ranged weapons.

sections.title: Shooting
lines: Fire any single weapon carried as a Combat Action. With an enemy within 3", you must target an enemy within that range.
Roll 1D6 + Combat Skill. To Hit: within 6" and in the open 3+; within weapon range and in the open 5+; within weapon range and in cover 6+.
Several shots may be resolved one at a time; if the target is destroyed, the next shot may go to another target within 3" of it.
Rapid Fire: every natural 6 allows an extra shot at the same target or a figure within 2". You may forgo it.
Malfunctions: a weapon that rolls two or more natural 1s in one round (firing and Rapid Fire dice together) is unusable. Restoring it takes a Combat Action and 1D6+Savvy scoring 7+.
Area weapons ignore Rapid Fire and Malfunctions. Roll a separately colored D6 with the shot: on a 1 the weapon is out of ammunition for the rest of the battle.

sections.title: Brawling
lines: Figures in base contact Brawl instead of firing. Troopers roll 1D6 + Combat Skill, +2 with a Melee weapon or +1 with a Pistol. Only one weapon bonus counts.
Enemies roll 1D6 + Combat Skill with no other modifiers.
The lower total takes a Hit; on a draw both take a Hit. An enemy rolling a natural 1 takes a Hit, and if it survives it rolls again immediately.
Damage is the highest of any Melee or Pistol weapon carried; with neither, Damage 0. Enemies use the Damage in their profile.
A character who eliminates their opponent may move 2" but cannot enter a new Brawl. An enemy that wins moves toward the nearest visible trooper, or into the defeated trooper's position.

sections.title: Resolving Hits
lines: Trooper armor saves on 5-6. A save shrugs off the Hit: the figure is not Stunned but is knocked back 1". Every damaging Hit on a trooper gets a save unless a rule says otherwise.
Otherwise roll 1D6 + Damage. Exceeds Toughness: casualty. Equal to Toughness: knocked back 1" and Wounded. Below Toughness: knocked back 1" and Stunned.
A Wounded trooper is at -1 to Brawling and cannot Dash, for the rest of the mission. A second Wound makes them a casualty.
A Wounded enemy falls and cannot move. A trooper moving within 1" of it is attacked in a Brawl. A second Wound kills it.
A figure with 3 Stun markers is knocked out. A Stunned figure in a Brawl fights at -1, and removes 1 Stun marker if it survives.

sections.title: Unusual Situations
lines: Brawl with two opponents: fight one chosen at random, then the other immediately, adding +1 to its Combat Skill.

Random moves are not slowed by Difficult terrain. Hitting a Linear, Block or Individual feature stops the move, and with more than 1" left the figure is Stunned. An enemy and a trooper moved into contact Brawl at Combat Skill +0, ignoring all modifiers.

Cover is made of people: if another trooper partly obscures the line of sight you may NOT fire, and Area weapons may not be fired so as to threaten other troopers. A target obscured by another enemy may be swapped, or the obscuring figure shot instead.
Equal options when moving an opponent: roll a D6, 1-3 for one, 4-6 for the other.

sections.title: Enemy Movement
lines: Enemies move in order of nearness to a player figure, at full Speed toward the nearest trooper by path, to fight a Brawl.
They know where every trooper is, ignore any trooper they have no path to, and may move through each other.
They take the path with better protection from fire if it is no slower, but never slow down just to take cover.
Nowhere to run: there is no morale system in Bug Hunt. The enemies keep coming until they are all destroyed.
A trooper may leave the battle across any battlefield edge, then rolls on the Lost Marine table (p.202).

sections.title: Spawn Points
lines: Used only when the mission's Spawn Rating is above 0. At the end of each round:
1. Reveal one unrevealed Spawn Point: make a random direction roll from the center and place it at the battlefield edge.
2. (Not in Round 1.) Lower every Countdown marker by 1. At 0, remove it and place a Contact marker on the Spawn Point.
3. Roll a D6 for each Spawn Point without a Countdown marker: 1-4 place a Countdown at that score; 5-6 none this round.
Closing a Spawn Point: a trooper within 3" who does not fire rolls 1D6+Savvy, 6+ removes it and its marker. One worker per point; one helper within 1" adds +1 and cannot fire either.

sections.title: Ending the Mission
lines: Two or more Objectives is a success; a Vital Objective counts 2 and a Critical Objective 3. With 4 or more signals at the start, investigate at least 2 before Evac or the total drops by 1.

From Round 5, a stationary, unstunned character taking no other action may request Evac: 2D6 + Objectives completed (packages held count), +1 if their Savvy is +1 or better. 10+: Evac arrives at the end of the next round. Otherwise roll again at the end of each round.
Place the landing marker; any trooper within 3" may leave the table. The ship leaves after 3 rounds. Each arrival raises the Priority by +1 for the rest of the mission.
While hovering, the drop ship fires two Light Machine Guns at +1 Combat Skill. They cannot malfunction.
No Objectives at all: the character in charge may face a court martial. D6, on a 1 they are removed from the campaign; 3 Reputation avoids it.
